correctness.rationale: The exact unit-step update maps to one of two labels. The probability of the bad transition from clean is exactly beta^k, and escape from bad is alpha^k. For summable entry probabilities, Borel--Cantelli bounds total bad entries; divergent escape probabilities preclude permanent bad residence. When both sums diverge, finite switching would imply an impossible permanent constant state. When both are summable, the expected total number of switches is finite and explicit infinite products give positive wrong-lock-in chance. The marginal recursion u_t=(1-s_t)u_(t-1)+s_t p_t/s_t and alpha>beta prove convergence in probability when escape sum diverges and k tends to infinity. Power-series comparison yields both strict critical constants and their endpoint conventions. The packaged program checks 952 finite rational/numerical identities without claiming to test infinite propositions.

value.rationale: The exact two-critical-value window identifies a nonmonotone tradeoff in how aggressively to increase robustness-screening workload for an actual minimum-loss SGD rule under fresh streaming corruption. It separates a.s. convergence from convergence in probability and establishes irreversible wrong-label freezing under oversized batches. This is a motivated, complete natural two-center classification and a sharp feasibility boundary, not an unmotivated parameter substitution or finite data-table entry. The model restrictions and absence of general algorithmic guarantees are explicitly stated.
